newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks fall, buyers abandon blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks fall, buyers abandon blue chips.

text.p: Jordanian shares slipped 0.66 percent on Sunday in subdued business, with institutional investors sidelined and blue-chip shares barely traded.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.9 points to 164.77 after turnover worth 933,000 dinars ($1.3 million).
Trading volume was dominated by block transfers of shares in two rarely traded stocks, Jordan Industrial Chemicals and General Mining.
Jordan Industrial rose 0.04 dinars to 4.77 dinars in trade worth 320,000 dinars in just a handful of transactions. General Mining fell 0.03 to 2.17 dinars.
Most trades were focused on two other small companies, Universal Modern Industries Co and National Chlorine, which registered strong gains to 1.16 and 1.47 dinars.
"The blue chips are quiet and there's only a few local investors buying," said analyst Mohammad Abdallah of Pearl Consulting. "There's no institutional demand."
Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the official index up to a three-year high earlier in July, lost two dinars to 289 in paltry trade of just 120 shares.
Local investors piled into the shares in recent weeks, anticipating strong 1997 profits, announcements of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
But cancellation of the 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling has been delayed in cabinet, deflating the Arab Bank bubble.
Overall 18 shares fell on Sunday and 14 rose. Another 18 traded but closed unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, fell 0.18 percent to 80.67 points, 3.27 percent down since the start of the year.
